questions.prompt: What is the range of a typical clinical thermometer?
questions.explain: Human body temperatures lie in a narrow range, so clinical thermometers measure only 35–42 °C, very precisely.

questions.prompt: Why shouldn't you use a clinical thermometer to measure boiling water?
options: Water is not allowed near it
Its range only goes up to 42 °C, and it could break
questions.explain: Above its range the liquid expands too much and the glass may crack.

questions.prompt: A doctor reads a fever of 102.2 °F. What is this in °C?
Match each temperature to what it describes.
questions.explain: These fixed points help you check your readings.

questions.prompt: Which are correct precautions when using a laboratory thermometer? Choose all that apply.
options: Keep the bulb fully in the liquid, not touching the container
Keep your eye level with the top of the liquid when reading
Wait until the reading stops changing
questions.explain: Holding the bulb adds your body heat; lab thermometers are not shaken (that's for clinical thermometers).

questions.prompt: Why are mercury thermometers being replaced by digital thermometers?
options: Mercury is toxic if the thermometer breaks
questions.explain: Mercury is poisonous and harms people and the environment when spilled. Digital thermometers are safer.

questions.prompt: Order the steps for using a clinical thermometer.
steps: Shake it until the reading is below 35 °C
Place the bulb under the tongue for about a minute
Take it out and read it, holding it by the far end
Wash it again and store it safely
questions.explain: Hygiene and shaking it down are important with clinical thermometers.
